findings.claim: PRD section 4 still describes the old storage model (one DB per MCP server, JSONL journal per agent session, single writer, 'No shared writable DB'), which ADR-0002 (Accepted, G21) replaced with one shared context.db per project.
findings.evidence: PRD-v2.md:75-80 'sessions/<server-id>.db ... single writer', 'journal/<agent-session-id>.jsonl', 'No shared writable DB -> removes #985 #880 #992 #905 #1205'; ADR-0002:17-19 'One SQLite file per project: .../context.db. Tables: events, sources, chunks (FTS5), meta'; README.md:79 agrees with ADR.
findings.fix: Rewrite PRD section 4 to the ADR-0002 layout. Re-map #985 #880 #992 #905 #1205 to the new mechanism (BEGIN IMMEDIATE + busy timeout, no spin loop) instead of 'no shared writable DB'. Drop owners/*.pid and the 14-day per-session-file cleanup or restate them as row-level retention.

findings.claim: ADR-0002 has no corruption policy. The only policy (PRD:84) says '--fix deletes only that session DB', which with one shared file deletes every session, worktree and agent of the project. It also names a 'context-mode doctor --fix' CLI that ADR-0002 item 3 says does not exist ('no CLI'). Open #867 (mid-session SQLITE_CORRUPT on a held handle) has no rule.
findings.evidence: PRD-v2.md:84 'Corruption: hard error ... context-mode doctor --fix ... deletes only that session DB (#867)'; ADR-0002:27 'No npm publish, no CLI'; tickets/data/isall.json #867 OPEN 'ContentStore self-heals DB corruption only at open-time (lossy recreate) - mid-session SQLITE_CORRUPT on a held handle is never caught'.
findings.fix: Add a Corruption section to ADR-0002: detect at open and mid-session; hard error with a ctx_doctor fix step (tool, not CLI); the fix renames context.db + -wal + -shm to .corrupt-<ts> (keeps evidence for the debug report) and states that all sessions of the project lose data.
findings.archaeology: INTRODUCED_BY 9e246a8e 2026-04-13 'fix: WAL checkpoint on exit + corrupt DB recovery (#244)', Closes #244 ('MCP server dies on heavy ctx_execute workloads'). ORIGINAL_INTENT: 'SessionDB renames corrupt files to .corrupt-{timestamp} for debugging; ContentStore deletes and recreates (ephemeral DB)'. v1 src/db-base.ts:474-484 renameCorruptDB covers '', '-wal', '-shm'. REGRESSION_RISK: a plain delete of context.db only (leaving -wal/-shm) or deleting without rename loses debug data and can re-trigger open failure. SAFE_FIX_CONSTRAINTS: keep the rename of all 3 files; no silent recreate (owner decision, PRD:84); keep v1 test 73635a0c 'cover withRetry, corruption predicate, and cleanup helpers (#292)' for the kept predicate.

findings.claim: ADR-0002 write rules drop two v1 fixes: WAL checkpoint(TRUNCATE) on close/exit and synchronous=NORMAL. verify-single-db consequence 3 requires 'WAL + synchronous=NORMAL', but the ADR does not even say journal_mode=WAL. With one file shared by many servers and hooks, an unbounded WAL is more likely than in v1.
findings.evidence: ADR-0002:20-24 lists only timeout 5000, BEGIN IMMEDIATE, 1 MB chunks, no retry; tickets/verify-single-db.md consequence 3 'WAL + synchronous=NORMAL'; v1 src/db-base.ts:343-344 and 397-399 'Checkpoint WAL before close to prevent contention on restart (#103)'.
findings.fix: Add to Decision 2: journal_mode=WAL, synchronous=NORMAL, PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE) (or PASSIVE when other connections are open) on server exit; hooks never checkpoint. Add a GP8 assertion: -wal size bounded after the run.
findings.archaeology: INTRODUCED_BY 939c5ca8 2026-03-13 'fix: add process lifecycle guard to prevent orphaned MCP servers (#103)' (closeDB checkpoint) and 9e246a8e 2026-04-13 (#244). ORIGINAL_INTENT (9e246a8e): 'Exit handler now calls closeDB() (WAL checkpoint + close) instead of bare db.close(), preventing orphaned WAL files that crash the next process on heavy workloads.' REGRESSION_RISK: v2 re-opens #244 if exit skips checkpoint. SAFE_FIX_CONSTRAINTS: checkpoint must not block hooks past the 40 ms budget; TRUNCATE needs no other readers, so use it only on last-writer exit.

findings.claim: No schema-version or migration rule for the shared DB, while ctx_doctor checks 'schema version' and the owner wants frequent releases. Two plugin versions (old server still running, new hook) will write the same context.db during an upgrade; nothing says what each does on a version mismatch.
findings.evidence: TECH-SPEC.md:226 'context.db: integrity_check, FTS5 integrity, schema version'; ADR-0002:18 'meta' table with no content defined; grep for user_version/migrat in TECH-SPEC, PRD and ADRs finds nothing.
findings.fix: Define in ADR-0002: PRAGMA user_version (or meta row) as schema version; additive-only migrations inside BEGIN IMMEDIATE at open; an older binary that sees a newer version opens read-only and returns a hard error with the upgrade step (no fallback).

findings.claim: 'No retry loop' is decided but the ADR does not say what happens when busy_timeout expires. verify-single-db consequences 5 and 6 say hooks must catch 'database is locked' and drop the event, and big server writes must run in a worker or small chunks because the sync wait blocks the event loop. Neither rule reached the ADR or a GP test.
findings.evidence: tickets/verify-single-db.md C3 'A lock held longer than the timeout fails with database is locked after about 5.2 s'; consequence 5 'Hooks must catch this and drop the event, not crash'; consequence 6 'Run them in a worker thread or in small chunks'; README.md:70 'Gemini and Copilot CLI block the tool when a hook fails, so hooks must never throw'; TECH-SPEC.md:294 GP8 tests only '0 busy errors'.
findings.fix: Add to Decision 2: hook on SQLITE_BUSY after timeout = drop event, exit 0, count it in meta for doctor; server tool on SQLITE_BUSY = hard error naming the lock, no retry. Add a GP8 case that holds a write lock 6 s and checks both outcomes.
findings.archaeology: INTRODUCED_BY 13dcec21 2026-04-02 'fix: handle SQLITE_BUSY with retry logic and graceful errors (closes #218)' (#218 CLOSED 'MCP server crashes under multi-session SQLite contention'). ORIGINAL_INTENT: graceful error instead of crash under contention. REGRESSION_RISK: deleting withRetry (correct, #985) without a defined busy outcome re-opens #218 crashes. SAFE_FIX_CONSTRAINTS: keep the 'graceful error, no crash' part of 13dcec21; drop only the spin at src/db-base.ts:446.

findings.claim: The DB path key is the git common dir hash, but the ADR does not say what happens when the project dir is not in a git repo (or git is missing). PRD makes global mode explicit only (E1), and 'no fallback chains' forbids silently using cwd.
findings.evidence: ADR-0002:17 '~/.context-mode/projects/<git-common-dir-hash>/context.db'; PRD-v2.md:155 'E1 Global mode CONTEXT_MODE_PROJECT=global, explicit only'; PRD-v2.md:74 same.
findings.fix: State the non-git rule in ADR-0002: key = hash of realpath of the project source dir, as one defined rule (not a fallback), or a hard error with the doctor step. Add a GP case for a non-git folder.

findings.claim: GP8 does not check the one rule that verify-single-db found makes busy_timeout useless: a deferred BEGIN that reads and then writes. v1 transaction() uses plain BEGIN, so code ported from v1 keeps this bug and GP8 load may not hit it.
findings.evidence: tickets/verify-single-db.md C3 'A deferred BEGIN that reads, then writes after another process commits, gets SQLITE_BUSY at once (0 ms)'; v1 src/db-base.ts:168 'this.#raw.exec("BEGIN")' (git blame 302bb7b8 2026-04-13).
findings.fix: Add a GP8 or unit assertion: every write path uses BEGIN IMMEDIATE (wrap in one store helper; test a read-then-write under a concurrent committer gets 0 busy errors).

covered: TECH-SPEC storage refs (doctor checks, GP8, S-NODE)
